chunks: And with this chain, from Abdul Adheem ibn Abdullah Al-Hasani, who said: I asked Muhammad ibn Ali Ar-Rida (peace be upon them both),
about His Exalted Saying, 'Woe to you, then woe; again, woe to you, then woe.' He said: 'Allah the Exalted says,
You became distant from the good of this world. You will also become distant from the good of the Hereafter.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Awlaa laka fa-awlaa' according to Imam Ar-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.) elucidates the repetitive emphasis in the Quranic phrase 'Awlaa laka fa-awlaa' as a profound declaration of estrangement, specifically interpreting it as being distant from the goodness of both the worldly life and the Hereafter. This exegesis highlights the comprehensive nature of divine punishment, where the afflicted are cut off from all sources of benefit, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing such verses as indicative of total spiritual and material loss for the heedless.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-205 According to the same documentation, Abdul Adheem ibn Abdullah Al-Hassani narrated that he asked Muhammad ibn Ali Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.)
about the Honorable the Exalted God’s words, ‘Woe be to thee, (O men!), yea, woe! Again, woe be to thee, (O men!), yea, woe!’ He (a.s.) replied, “The Honorable the Exalted God says,
‘You became distant from the good of this world. You will also become distant from the good of the Hereafter.’”
